Cultured

KUL-churd -- two syllables, stress on the first syllable, KUL. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Cultured is educated, polished, and refined.

Years of reading and travel made Uncle Theo surprisingly cultured for a tugboat captain.

Worked Example

On the class trip, one exchange student quietly names the sculptor of the fountain, explains why the cathedral's windows glow blue at dusk, and hums the opera the street musician is playing -- never showing off, just at home in all of it.

That student is cultured: educated, polished, and refined, comfortable with art, music, and ideas. Cultured describes taste and knowledge grown over time -- like a garden, it has been deliberately tended.

How Cultured Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

refined

refined: polished in taste and manners

sophisticated

sophisticated: worldly and knowledgeable

genteel

genteel: elegantly polite and well-bred

Antonyms

crude

crude: rough and unpolished

boorish

boorish: rude and ill-mannered

How Strong Is It? — refined → cultured → sophisticated

refined vs. cultured

refined vs. cultured: Refined covers manners and taste -- a refined guest handles the formal dinner smoothly -- while cultured adds the library and the concert hall: knowledge of art and ideas, not just polish.

sophisticated vs. cultured

sophisticated vs. cultured: Sophisticated is the strongest and worldliest: a cultured reader knows the symphony's history, while a sophisticated traveler seems to know every city, custom, and menu on the continent.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of cultured.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — cult-

root — cult-: to till, to tend, to care for (Latin colere, cultus)

suffix — -ured

suffix — -ured: having been given the quality of (Latin -ura plus English -ed)

Put it together

Put it together: Cultured grows from Latin colere, 'to till and tend the soil.' A cultured mind is a cultivated field: someone spent years planting it with books, music, and art and tending what grew. The farming metaphor survives in both 'culture' and 'agriculture.'

Use the root in a new word: cultivate

Use the root in a new word: cultivate: The club was founded to cultivate a love of chess among younger students.

Word Choice

Cultured praises a person's tended mind and manners: a cultured host, a cultured ear. Watch the lab-and-kitchen senses that share the spelling -- cultured pearls and cultured yogurt are 'grown under controlled conditions,' a literal cousin of the same tending idea. On the ISEE, applied to a person, cultured means educated, polished, and refined.
